title_ar: Backend بالعمق: Java وJDBC والـconnection pool وSpring Boot والـsaga
title_en: Backend in depth: Java, collections and streams, JDBC and transactions, connection pools, Spring Boot, concurrency, saga

storyboard_notes.text: DD-P14 is the Java dive with no Java in the trunk. The framing card sets the context ('DD-P14 · Backend from the inside'), with a visual bridge from the trunk's nearest backend or API mention (CH-21 and the API chapters). Placement does not move.

sentences.ar: النهارده إحنا هندخل في رحلة ممتعة جدا جوا تفاصيل الـbackend المعقدة
sentences.en: Today we go on a really fun trip inside the complex details of the backend.

sentences.ar: هنتتبع بالزبط خطوة بخطوة رحلة أي request من أول ما بيسيب العميل لحد ما يغوص في أعماق الـdatabase ويرجع تاني
sentences.en: We will trace, exactly step by step, the journey of any request from the moment it leaves the client until it dives deep into the database and comes back.

sentences.ar: الموضوع مش مجرد خط مستقيم لا خالص
sentences.en: It is not just a straight line, not at all.

sentences.ar: دي رحلة مليانة مطبات وتفاصيل تقنية هتعجبكو جدا
sentences.en: It is a journey full of bumps and technical details you will really like.

sentences.ar: أولاً رحلة الـrequest وحروب اللغات ثانياً هنشوف شوية في خخص الريا في Java والـStreams
sentences.en: First, the request journey and the language wars; second, we look at some (unclear) in Java and the Streams.

sentences.ar: ثالثاً الـJDBC والـtransactions رابعاً هنوقف عند الـConnection Pool خامساً طبقات الـSpring Boot
sentences.en: Third, JDBC and transactions; fourth, we stop at the connection pool; fifth, the Spring Boot layers.

sentences.ar: وأخيراً هنختم بالـconcurrency والـsaga pattern
sentences.en: And finally we close with concurrency and the saga pattern.

sentences.ar: تمام جداً يلا بينا نبدأ بأول محطة معنا
sentences.en: Great, let us start with our first station.

sentences.ar: رحلة الـrequest وحروب اللغات اللي دايماً دايرة في طبقة دي
sentences.en: The request journey and the language wars that always go on in this layer.

sentences.ar: تخيلوا معايا كده الخريطة المكانية للـrequest
sentences.en: Picture with me the spatial map of the request.

sentences.ar: بيبدأ الأول يخبط على باب الـController اللي بيستقبله ويوجهه
sentences.en: It first knocks on the door of the Controller, which receives it and routes it.

sentences.ar: بعدين ينزل للـService ودي بقى اللي فيها كل الـbusiness rules
sentences.en: Then it goes down to the Service, which holds all the business rules.

sentences.ar: ومنها للـRepository اللي بيكتب الـSQL لحد ما نوصل للـConnection Pool ومنه أخيراً للـdatabase
sentences.en: From there to the Repository, which writes the SQL, until we reach the connection pool and finally the database.

sentences.ar: الفكرة الجوهرية هنا إن كل الطبقات دي معتمدة على بعض بشكل رأسي بالزبط
sentences.en: The core idea here is that all these layers depend on each other vertically.

sentences.ar: يعني لو حصلت أي مشكلة صغيرة في الـConnection Pool كل حاجة فوق بتقف تماماً والسيستم كله بيقع
sentences.en: So if any small problem happens in the connection pool, everything above stops completely and the whole system goes down.

sentences.ar: بصوا بقى على المقارنة المباشرة دي بين Python وJava لتنفيذ نفس المهمة حاجة فعلا مثيرة للاهتمام
sentences.en: Now look at this direct comparison between Python and Java doing the same task; it is really interesting.

sentences.ar: Python بتدي لك كود مختصر جدا حوالي 20 سطر مع dynamic typing
sentences.en: Python gives you very short code, about 20 lines, with dynamic typing.

sentences.ar: بس في نفس الوقت هي محكومة بحاجة اسمها الـGIL
sentences.en: But at the same time it is constrained by something called the GIL.

sentences.ar: على ناحية التانية هتلاقي Java ممكن الكود يوصل لـ80 سطر أو أكتر
sentences.en: On the other side, Java code can reach 80 lines or more.

sentences.ar: بس بتعوضك بـstatic typing بيصطاد أخطاء بدري جدا
sentences.en: But it makes up for it with static typing that catches errors very early.

sentences.ar: وبتشتغل على JVM مع JIT Compiler بيدي سرعة خرافية
sentences.en: And it runs on the JVM with a JIT compiler that gives tremendous speed.

sentences.ar: والأهم من كل ده True Multi Threading
sentences.en: And most important of all: true multithreading.

sentences.ar: يعني لما نيجي نبني Systems بتتعامل مع مليارات السجلات في الـproduction scale الـarchitecture دي بتعمل فرق مش طبيعي
sentences.en: When we build systems handling billions of records at production scale, this architecture makes a huge difference.

sentences.ar: طيب بناء على الكلام ده خلونا ندخل جوه طبقة الـService ونكشف شوية خبايا وفخاخ برمجية موجودة في Java
sentences.en: Based on that, let us go inside the Service layer and uncover some hidden programming traps in Java.

sentences.ar: هنا بقى عندنا فخ عبقري جدا ممكن يوقع أي حد
sentences.en: Here we have a really clever trap that can catch anyone.

sentences.ar: لو كتبنا في الكود Integer 127 يساوي يساوي 127 النتيجة هتطلع true عادي جدا
sentences.en: If we write Integer 127 == 127 in code, the result is true, as expected.

sentences.ar: بس لو كتبنا Integer 128 يساوي يساوي 128 النتيجة فجأة بتبقى false ازاي؟
sentences.en: But if we write Integer 128 == 128, the result suddenly becomes false. How?

sentences.ar: السر كله في حاجة اسمها الـInteger cache الـJVM بيخزن الأرقام من سالب 128 لحد 127 مسبقا
sentences.en: The whole secret is the Integer cache: the JVM pre-stores numbers from -128 to 127.

sentences.ar: فأي مقارنة بينهم بعلامة يساوي يساوي بتنجح
sentences.en: So any == comparison between them succeeds.

sentences.ar: لكن رقم 128 ده بيتعامل كـobject جديد تماماً في الزاكرة
sentences.en: But 128 is treated as a completely new object in memory.

sentences.ar: عشان كده القاعدة الزهبية هنا عشان نتجنب كوارث في الكود دايماً نستخدم دالة .equals في المقارنات بدل علامة اليساوي
sentences.en: So the golden rule to avoid disasters in code: always use .equals in comparisons instead of the == sign.

sentences.ar: ولو جينا نتكلم عن الـJava Streams API فهي بتشتغل بعبقرية كأنها بالضبط البديل لـpandas في Python
sentences.en: And the Java Streams API works brilliantly, exactly like the equivalent of pandas in Python.

sentences.ar: بنقدر نعمل بيها سلسلة عمليات وراء بعض بمنتهى السهولة زي الـfilter والـmap والـgroupingBy والـsum نفس قوة ونفس المرونة
sentences.en: We can chain operations one after another very easily, like filter, map, groupingBy and sum, with the same power and flexibility.

sentences.ar: فخ تاني هنا لو استخدمته Parallel Stream على data sets صغيرة الأداء بيبقى أبطأ مش أسرع زي ما أنتم متخيلين
sentences.en: Another trap: if you use a parallel stream on small data sets, performance gets slower, not faster as you imagine.

sentences.ar: وده لأن تكلفة تقسيم الشغلة على Threads بتكون أكبر من وقت التنفيذ نفسه
sentences.en: That is because the cost of splitting the work across threads is bigger than the execution time itself.

sentences.ar: ودلوقتي يلا بينا ننزل أعمق شوية لطبقة الـRepository وتحديداً المحطة الثالثة رحلة الـJDBC والـtransactions
sentences.en: Now let us go a bit deeper to the Repository layer, specifically the third station: the JDBC journey and transactions.

sentences.ar: الخطوات هنا واضحة ومباشرة جداً
sentences.en: The steps here are clear and very direct.

sentences.ar: بنبدأ نفتح الـconnection وبعدين نعمل PreparedStatement بننفذ الـquery وبنمشي على النتائج من خلال الـResultSet
sentences.en: We open the connection, then create a PreparedStatement, execute the query, and walk through the results via the ResultSet.

sentences.ar: بس ركزوا معايا الخطوة الأهمة على الإطلاق هنا هي PreparedStatement
sentences.en: But focus with me: the most important step of all here is the PreparedStatement.

sentences.ar: ليه؟ لأنه ده اللي بيعمل block كامل لأي هجمات SQL Injection لأنه بيفصل البيانات عن الكود تماما
sentences.en: Why? Because it completely blocks any SQL injection attacks, since it separates the data from the code entirely.

sentences.ar: وكمان بنستخدم try-with-resources عشان نقفل الـconnection بشكل أوتوماتيكي وما يحصلش عندنا أي تسريب للـresources
sentences.en: We also use try-with-resources to close the connection automatically so no resources leak.

sentences.ar: وهنا بقى بيجي الأكشن الحقيقي بتاع الـtransaction إحنا بنوقف الـauto commit ونبدأ السيناريو
sentences.en: Here comes the real transaction action: we turn off auto commit and start the scenario.

sentences.ar: مندخل طلب جديد وبنحاول نخصم من المخزون بس بنحط شرط زكي جدا
sentences.en: We insert a new order and try to deduct from stock, but we add a very smart condition.

sentences.ar: where stock أكبر من أو يساوي question mark
sentences.en: The condition read aloud: where stock is greater than or equal to question mark.

sentences.ar: لو الشرط ده متحققش والمخزون ما كانش كفاية العملية كلها بتقف وبنعمل rollback فوري
sentences.en: If that condition is not met and the stock was not enough, the whole operation stops and we roll back immediately.

sentences.ar: الـrollback ده عامل كأنه بيرجع الزمن لورا كأن الطلب ما حصلش من الأساس
sentences.en: That rollback is like turning time back, as if the order never happened at all.

sentences.ar: وده بيحمينا تماما من أي مشاكل race conditions لو في كذا طلب دخلوا في نفس اللحظة
sentences.en: And it fully protects us from race condition problems if several orders come in at the same moment.

sentences.ar: المحطة الرابعة اللي جايين عليها دلوقتي هي البنية تحتية الحرجة جدا الـConnection Pool
sentences.en: The fourth station we are reaching now is the very critical infrastructure: the connection pool.

sentences.ar: شايفين رقم 10 ده؟
sentences.en: See this number 10?

sentences.ar: ده مش مجرد رقم ده أقصى عدد connections في إعدادات زي HikariCP كمثال
sentences.en: It is not just a number; it is the maximum number of connections in a config like HikariCP, for example.

sentences.ar: تخيلوا معي السيناريو ده 10 اتصالات كلهم مسحوبين ومشغولين في طلبات تانية
sentences.en: Imagine this scenario: 10 connections, all checked out and busy with other requests.

sentences.ar: فجأة يجي request رقم 11 يعمل إيه؟ بيقف في طابور يستنى؟
sentences.en: Suddenly request number 11 arrives; what does it do? Wait in a queue?

sentences.ar: لو وقت الـtimeout عدى من غير ما أي اتصال يفضى
sentences.en: If the timeout passes without any connection freeing up...

sentences.ar: بوم بنخبط في حيطة سد وبناخد error قاتل اسمه Pool Exhausted
sentences.en: Boom, we hit a dead-end wall and get a fatal error called pool exhausted.

sentences.ar: في اللحظة دي السيستم كله بيتشل لأن ببساطة مفيش أي مخرج للـdatabase
sentences.en: At that moment the whole system is paralyzed, simply because there is no way out to the database.

sentences.ar: وعشان نريح نفسنا من كتابة كل الشغل اليدوي ده في كل مرة بندخل على المحطة الخامسة طبقات Spring Boot
sentences.en: To spare ourselves writing all this manual work every time, we move to the fifth station: the Spring Boot layers.

sentences.ar: هنا بنشوف السحر الحقيقي لـSpring Boot إزاي بيغلف كل الرحلة اللي حكيناها دي بمجرد Annotations بسيطة
sentences.en: Here we see the real magic of Spring Boot: how it wraps the whole journey we described with just simple annotations.

sentences.ar: بنحط @Entity عشان نوصف في الجدول وبنستخدم JpaRepository عشان يكتب هو الـqueries نيابة عننا
sentences.en: We put @Entity to describe the table, and use JpaRepository so it writes the queries for us.

sentences.ar: وبنحط @Service مع @Transactional عشان نديل قواعد الـbusiness والـrollbacks بمنتهى الأناقة
sentences.en: And we put @Service with @Transactional to handle the business rules and rollbacks elegantly.

sentences.ar: وأخيراً @RestController عشان API Routing
sentences.en: And finally @RestController for API routing.

sentences.ar: طبقات مترتبة ومتنظمة بتربط كل خطوة بأقل مجهود ممكن
sentences.en: Ordered, organized layers that connect each step with minimal effort.

sentences.ar: بس خدوا بالكو السهولة دي بتيجي معاها مسئولية وفخاخ برضو
sentences.en: But watch out: this ease comes with responsibility, and traps too.

sentences.ar: الحاجة الممتازة هنا هي GlobalExceptionHandler وده مكان مركزي بيوحد الردود
sentences.en: The great thing here is the GlobalExceptionHandler, a central place that unifies the responses.

sentences.ar: يعني يرجع لك 404 لو مش موجود أو 409 لو فيه تعارض أو 500 كخطأ داخلي
sentences.en: It returns 404 if something is not found, 409 if there is a conflict, or 500 as an internal error.

sentences.ar: لكن الفخ المرعب بجد هو الـJPA N+1 query trap بسبب ميزة اسمها lazy loading
sentences.en: But the truly scary trap is the JPA N+1 query trap, caused by a feature called lazy loading.

sentences.ar: لو عندنا مثلاً 100 سجل بدل ما السيستم يعمل استعلام واحد لا ده بيعمل استعلام أساسي وبعدين 100 استعلام فرعي لكل سجل الواحده
sentences.en: If we have, say, 100 records, instead of one query the system runs a main query and then 100 sub-queries, one per record.

sentences.ar: يعني 101 query عشان بس 100 سجل
sentences.en: That is 101 queries just for 100 records.

sentences.ar: متخيلين ده بيدمر الأداء ازاي؟
sentences.en: Can you imagine how this destroys performance?

sentences.ar: ودلوقتي بنوصل لذروة الشرح بتاعنا المحطة السادسة الـconcurrency والـsaga pattern
sentences.en: Now we reach the climax of our explainer: the sixth station, concurrency and the saga pattern.

sentences.ar: لما نيجي نقارن الـconcurrency بنلاقي إن Python بتعتمد على شوية حيل زي الـthreading للـI/O أو multiprocessing للـCPU أو asyncio
sentences.en: Comparing concurrency, Python relies on a few tricks: threading for I/O, multiprocessing for CPU, or asyncio.

sentences.ar: وده كله عشان تلف وتدور حوالين قيود الـGIL
sentences.en: All of that is to work around the limits of the GIL.

sentences.ar: لكن في Java الوضع مختلف إحنا هنا بنتكلم عن True Multi -Core Multi -Threading
sentences.en: But in Java it is different: we are talking about true multi-core multithreading.

sentences.ar: الـthreads بتشتغل بجد على كذا core في نفس اللحظة
sentences.en: Threads really run on several cores at the same moment.

sentences.ar: بس طبعا القوة دي مش مجانية بتتطلب حذر شديد وحماية صارمة للبيانات المشتركة باستخدام الـatomic safety عشان نضمن إن ما يحصلش أي تداخل
sentences.en: Of course this power is not free: it needs great caution and strict protection of shared data using atomic safety, so no interference happens.

sentences.ar: طيب لما الشغل بيكبر وبيبقى متوزع على كذا microservice وكل واحدة ليها الـdatabase الخاصة بيها ما بقاش ينفع نعمل transaction واحدة وrollback عادي
sentences.en: When the work grows and is spread over several microservices, each with its own database, a single transaction and a normal rollback no longer work.

sentences.ar: هنا بقى بيظهر بطل اسمه الـsaga pattern
sentences.en: Here a hero called the saga pattern appears.

sentences.ar: الفكرة إننا بنمشي لقدام بنحجز المخزون وبعدين ندفع
sentences.en: The idea is we move forward: reserve stock, then pay.

sentences.ar: بس لو جينا في خطوة الشحنة وحصلت مشكلة وفشلت بنبدأ نشغل العمليات العكسية بالعكس أو اللي بنسميه compensation
sentences.en: But if the shipping step hits a problem and fails, we run the reverse operations in reverse order, what we call compensation.

sentences.ar: يعني رجع الفلوس الأول وبعدين نلغي حجز المخزون
sentences.en: That is, refund the money first, then cancel the stock reservation.

sentences.ar: دي الطريقة الوحيدة عشان نضمن التناسق في الأنظمة الموزعة المعقدة دي
sentences.en: This is the only way to guarantee consistency in these complex distributed systems.

sentences.ar: بعد ما لفنا اللفة دي كلها وشفنا التفاصيل من أول الـConnection Pool لحد الـsaga pattern والعمليات العكسية بنوصل لسؤال مهم جداً بيفرض نفسه
sentences.en: After this whole tour, from the connection pool to the saga pattern and compensating operations, an important question arises.

sentences.ar: إزاي نقدر ندير كل الـdata pipelines المعقدة والموزعة دي بشكل موثوق على مستوى الـenterprise scale
sentences.en: How can we manage all these complex, distributed data pipelines reliably at enterprise scale?

sentences.ar: إزاي نضمن إن كل حاجة بتحصل في وقتها وبالترتيب المظبوط؟
sentences.en: How do we make sure everything happens on time and in the right order?

sentences.ar: ده بالضبط السؤال اللي حيفتح لنا الباب عشان نستكشف عالم الـETLs والـDAGs في المرحلة الجاية
sentences.en: That is exactly the question that opens the door to exploring the world of ETLs and DAGs in the next stage.

glossary.rule: Explain the term in Egyptian Arabic the first time it appears; then use the original term naturally, in Latin script, inside Arabic sentences.
glossary.register_ar: Natural Egyptian, clear, calm, professional. Use إحنا and خلّينا نشوف and ببساطة where they help. No heavy Modern Standard Arabic. No exaggerated slang. Numbers are spoken naturally in Egyptian but displayed as Western digits.
glossary.register_en: Plain, direct, unhurried. Short sentences. No hype, no "imagine that…", no rhetorical questions that are not real prediction prompts. Say the number, then pause for half a beat before the next sentence — the pause is where the viewer reads the screen.
glossary.never_translate_rule: Explain them in Egyptian Arabic the first time they appear, then use the original term naturally.
glossary.on_screen: Western digits, Latin terms in LTR isolates, Egyptian Arabic copy (no MSA), no per-letter animation (04 section 3.4).

concepts.def_en: An organized store of data managed by software that lets many users and programs safely read, write and query it.
concepts.failure: Treating a database as a bigger spreadsheet, ignoring keys, constraints and concurrent writes.

concepts.def_en: A statically typed, object-oriented language that runs on the JVM; used for large backend systems, APIs and big-data tooling.
concepts.failure: Ignoring null handling, leading to NullPointerException at runtime.

concepts.def_en: Java's standard API for databases: open a connection, create a statement, execute, walk the results, then close everything.
concepts.failure: Leaving connections open after errors, exhausting the database's connection limit.

concepts.def_en: Java framework (Spring Boot) that wires app layers together with annotations: controller, service, repository, handling dependencies and transactions.
concepts.failure: Putting business logic in controllers instead of the service layer.

concepts.def_en: A pattern for work spanning several services and databases: each step has a compensating action that undoes it if a later step fails.
concepts.failure: Expecting a saga to roll back atomically; compensations run later and may fail too.

concepts.def_en: In Git, a project with its full version history that others can clone. In design, a class hiding how data is stored.
concepts.failure: Committing secrets, large data or generated files into the repository.

concepts.def_en: Structured Query Language: the standard declarative language for querying and changing data in relational databases by describing what you want.
concepts.failure: Thinking SQL runs in written order; the engine plans execution in its own order.

concepts.def_en: A readable, general-purpose programming language widely used for data analysis, automation, pipelines and AI work.
concepts.failure: Using plain loops over huge data instead of vectorized pandas or SQL operations.

concepts.def_en: The Java Virtual Machine runs compiled bytecode on any operating system, using a JIT compiler to speed up hot code.
concepts.failure: Comparing boxed Integers with == works for small values but fails for larger ones.

concepts.def_en: The live environment where real users and real data are served, so changes there carry real consequences.
concepts.failure: Testing or editing directly in production, risking accidental data changes and outages.

concepts.def_en: Application Programming Interface: a defined contract through which one program requests data or actions from another, often over HTTP using JSON.
concepts.failure: Changing a response field or meaning without versioning, breaking every client that depends on it.

concepts.def_en: A Python library for tabular data analysis, built around the DataFrame, for loading, cleaning, filtering, grouping and joining data in memory.
concepts.failure: Loading data bigger than RAM into pandas, or looping row by row instead of vectorizing.

concepts.def_en: A request to a database or search system to fetch, filter or change data; in SQL, usually a SELECT statement.
concepts.failure: Blaming hardware for a slow query when a full table scan is the cause.

concepts.def_en: An attack where untrusted input is executed as code or commands, such as SQL injection; parameterized queries keep data separate from code.
concepts.failure: Building queries by concatenating user input into SQL strings instead of parameterizing.

concepts.def_en: A Java block that automatically closes opened resources, such as connections, when it ends, even if an error occurs.
concepts.failure: Opening connections without it, so errors leak them until the pool runs out.

concepts.def_en: A group of database operations treated as one unit: either all succeed together or none take effect.
concepts.failure: Leaving a transaction open too long, holding locks and blocking other sessions.

concepts.def_en: In git, a saved snapshot of changes with a message; in databases, the step that makes a transaction permanent.
concepts.failure: Committing unrelated changes together with vague messages, making review and rollback hard.

concepts.def_en: Reverting to a previous known-good state: undoing a failed transaction's changes, or redeploying the last good version.
concepts.failure: Assuming a code rollback also undoes database changes already committed.

concepts.def_en: A maximum time to wait for an operation; when it passes, the operation is aborted or fails instead of waiting forever.
concepts.failure: No timeout set, so one stuck call holds a connection or worker forever.

concepts.def_en: A message or failure signalling that something went wrong; read it first, since it usually names the cause and the location.
concepts.failure: Pasting the error into a search engine without first reading the terminal output.

concepts.def_en: Java Persistence API: a standard for mapping Java classes to database tables so you work with objects instead of hand-written SQL.
concepts.failure: Ignoring lazy loading, which triggers the N+1 query trap in loops.

concepts.def_en: The processor that executes program instructions one after another, extremely fast, reading data from memory.
concepts.failure: Blaming the CPU for slowness actually caused by waiting on disk or memory.

concepts.def_en: A chain of automated steps where each stage's output feeds the next, such as extract, transform and load for data.
concepts.failure: Not making steps idempotent, so a rerun duplicates or corrupts data.

concepts.def_en: Extract, Transform, Load: pull data from sources, clean and reshape it first, then load the finished result into the target.
concepts.failure: Discarding the raw data after transforming, so mistakes cannot be replayed.

Fix beat: the target settles into place with a settle chime.
The shot camera: move + ease + intensity; drift always on; optional impact nudges (<= 4 px) on anchors.
Match cut between a layer of this shot and one of the next.
Lower-third caption for a source, term, speaker or location.
Draw an SVG path (stroke reveal; RTL by default for Arabic layouts).
Stacked layers (docker image, OSI, model, generic); cached layers glow.
A connection pool as a taxi rank; requests queue when exhausted.
Threads racing on shared state; a lock serialises them.
Saga steps with compensations that run backwards on failure.
